# Working-tree overlay seam: treating the semantic index as a stale baseline a coding agent patches at read time (DESIGN ONLY)

## What this is

The semantic index is a batch artifact built at a commit (`semantic/generations/<commit>-<tree>/semantic.sqlite`).
A coding agent's job is to *change code*, so the index is **always stale relative to the working tree** —
on a live branch `entire brain status` reports `freshness: unsafe` the moment the agent edits a file, and
a full reindex is too slow to run between tool calls. Today the read surfaces resolve symbols against the
index (`semanticSymbolsForFiles` → `findSemanticSymbolsForFilesSQLite` in `internal/cli/semantic.go`), so a
fact's locus, an impact traversal, or `inspect changes` can be answered against code that no longer matches
disk.

This note describes the intended fix: stop treating index freshness as a precondition and instead treat the
index as an **immutable global baseline** that a **session-scoped working-tree overlay** patches at read
time. The overlay is bounded by the diff — which the agent itself produced — not by repo size.

This is **DESIGN ONLY**; nothing below is implemented. It depends on one provider-side capability that does
not exist yet (see *Provider dependency*).

## The model: baseline ⊕ overlay

```
effective graph = index (global, as of commit C)  ⊕  fresh-parse(working-tree diff)
```

The fresh parse *overrides* the index for files in the current diff; the index supplies everything else.
The freshness gap is exactly the set of files in `git status` — which is exactly what `changedSemanticFiles`
(`internal/cli/semantic.go`) already computes for `inspect changes`. The agent does not need to discover
what is stale; it knows, because it made the edits.

## The definition/relation asymmetry (decides what a fresh parse can return)

A fresh parse of a changed file is not symmetric across record types:

- **Definition / signature / outbound edges** of a changed symbol — a single-file parse returns these
  *exactly and completely*. Cheap, high-value, no index needed.
- **Inbound edges** (who calls the changed symbol) — a single-file parse **cannot** return these; the caller
  set is global, which is what the index is for. The saving grace: a *new* inbound edge can only originate
  from another changed file, which is already in the diff. Unchanged callers' edges remain valid in the
  index.

# Multiplayer agent awareness: Phase 0 and Phase 1 (DESIGN ONLY)

Status: proposed, 2026-10-03. Nothing below is implemented.
Decision record: [`docs/adr/0001-multiplayer-agent-awareness-ownership.md`](adr/0001-multiplayer-agent-awareness-ownership.md).
Upstream asks: [`docs/multiplayer_cli_phase0_asks.md`](multiplayer_cli_phase0_asks.md).

## Why

Several coding agents now routinely work in one repository at the same time: parallel sessions
in sibling worktrees, background subagents, and Claude Code and Codex side by side. Brain
cannot see any of them until their work is committed as a checkpoint. Sessions are read only from
committed checkpoint refs (`internal/cli/export.go:41-50`), and live state is computed for the
caller's own worktree only (`brainLiveStateReport`, `internal/cli/agent_surface.go:4735`).

The release copy says this plainly: "Do not claim multi-agent collaboration is complete"
(`docs/release_press_release.md:138`), and it lists "multi-agent write coordination beyond local
safety" as future work (`:171`).

The most common collision is also the cheapest to catch. Two live agents on one machine edit the same
file or symbol, and neither knows until merge. Phase 1 targets exactly that case.

## Goals (Phase 0 + Phase 1)

1. **See** every live agent session on this machine for this repository, across all worktrees,
   including subagents nested under their parent.
2. **Know what each is changing**, from observed evidence (the worktree diff, mapped to symbols
   with Graph), not from self-reported lists.
3. **Warn** at the two moments that change a decision:
   - `brief`, with a "Concurrent work" section;
   - `hook pre-edit`, when the file is dirty in another live session.
4. Expose the same view as `entire brain agents [--json]` and the MCP tool `brain_agents`.

## Non-goals (deferred to later phases)

- Declared or advisory claims (`brain claim`). That is Phase 2.
- Cross-machine or team presence, and any data leaving the machine. That is Phase 3.
- Enforcement or locking of any kind. Warnings are advisory (see the ADR).
- Orchestration or work splitting. That is Phase 4.
- A second session tracker inside Brain. Identity and presence belong to the Entire CLI (see the ADR).

## Model: five layers, two in scope

| Layer | Question | Owner | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identity | Who is this actor (session, parent, agent, model, worktree)? | Entire CLI | 0 (asks), 1 (consume) |
| Presence | Is it alive right now? | Entire CLI, plus Brain-side derivation | 1 |
| Intent | What is it changing? | Brain (diff → Graph symbols) | 1 (observed only) |
| Coordination | Does that overlap with me? | Brain | 1 (warn), 2 (claims) |
| Collaboration | Handoff, shared notes, subagent result merge | Brain | 2+ |

### Identity record

```jsonc
{
  "session_id": "083bcf79-…",            // Entire session id
  "parent_session_id": null,              // set for subagents (derived in Phase 1; see adapter)
  "continues_session_id": "54c0e4d4-…",   // CLI ask (d); null until it ships
  "agent_id": "ade8c9b2eec7e9193",        // host subagent id (subagents only)
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01E19…",          // links to checkpoint IsTask/ToolUseID (export.go:3798-3799)
  "kind": "session" | "subagent",
  "agent": "Claude Code", "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "subagent_type": "Explore",
  "description": "Map multi-agent primitives in brain",
  "branch": "feat/linear-issue-memory",
  "worktree": "C:/…/entire-brain/.claude/worktrees/trail197-findings",
  "worktree_confidence": "verified" | "reported"
}
```

`worktree_confidence` exists because the CLI-reported `worktree_path` can be wrong. Session
`586a7064` ran in `.claude/worktrees/trail197-findings` on branch `fix/trail197-findings`, yet its
state file reports the main checkout path. Brain verifies the path by matching the session's branch
against `git worktree list --porcelain`. When the two disagree, the branch match wins, and the
result is marked `reported` when it cannot be verified.

### Presence

Derived. No new daemon and no heartbeat writer in Phase 1.

| State | Rule |
|---|---|
| `active` | CLI status `active`, or `last_interaction_time` within 2 minutes |
| `idle` | Not ended, and last interaction within the stale window (default 30 minutes, `--stale-after`) |
| `stale` | Not ended, but older than the stale window. Shown only with `--all`. Never triggers warnings. |
| `ended` | `ended_at` is set. Hidden unless `--all`. |

Subagents inherit their parent's presence, and are `active` while the parent is not ended and the
subagent has no trustworthy `completed_at`. CLI ask (b) explains why `completed_at` is untrusted
today. Expiry by timeout, not by an end event, is deliberate: sessions crash and never send one.
This mirrors the stale rule in `memoryCoordinatorHealth` (`internal/cli/memory_coordinator.go:175-190`).

### Intent (observed)

For each distinct live worktree, Brain computes:

1. **Changed files.** This reuses the `brainLiveStateReport` machinery: `git status --porcelain`,
   filtered by `loadBrainIgnore`, plus `git diff --shortstat HEAD`. It is generalized to take any
   worktree path rather than only the caller's.
2. **Changed symbols.** Changed files map to entities through Graph's working-tree entity diff
   for that worktree (`entire graph diff`, working tree, not `--head`). Brain also uses the
   `changedSemanticFiles` path where an index exists. If Graph is unavailable, the result stays at
   file level with `granularity: "file"`.
3. **Task text.** From the CLI `last_prompt` for sessions and `task_description` for subagents.
   It is truncated to 120 characters and passed through the existing privacy exclusions.

**Brain never uses CLI `files_touched` or task-record `files` in Phase 1.** Both are wrong today
(see CLI ask (c)). Intent is attributed to a *worktree*, not to a session. When several live
sessions share one worktree, they share its diff, and the output says so (`shared_worktree: true`).
That limit is accepted for Phase 1.

## Interface

### `entire brain agents [--json] [--all] [--stale-after 30m] [--no-symbols]`

The human output is a tree grouped by worktree:

```
worktree .claude/worktrees/trail197-findings  (fix/trail197-findings)  4 files dirty
  ● 586a7064  Claude Code · opus-5-5  idle 12m  "resolve trail 197 review findings"
      changes: internal/issues/store.go (Import, State), internal/cli/issues.go (+2)
worktree .  (feat/linear-issue-memory)  1 file dirty
  ● 41205a80  Claude Code · opus-5-5  active  "open trail status + multiplayer"   ← you
      └ fork ab87ba50  "Finish trail 197 findings"  running
overlaps: none
```

The `--json` schema (`brain.agents/v1`):

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "brain.agents/v1",
  "generated_at": "…",
  "self_session_id": "41205a80-…",          // from ENTIRE_SESSION_ID / `entire session current`
  "source": { "cli_version": "0.11.3", "adapter": "state-files" | "cli-json", "warnings": [] },
  "worktrees": [{
    "path": "…", "branch": "…", "head": "…",
    "dirty": true, "changed_files": ["…"],
    "changed_symbols": [{ "file": "…", "name": "Import", "kind": "method", "change": "modified" }],
    "granularity": "symbol" | "file",
    "sessions": ["586a7064-…"], "shared_worktree": false
  }],
  "agents": [ /* identity record + */ {
    "presence": "active" | "idle" | "stale" | "ended",
    "last_interaction_at": "…", "children": ["<agent ids>"]
  }],
  "overlaps": [{

| Intent | What is it changing? | Brain (diff → Graph symbols) | 1 (observed only) |
| Coordination | Does that overlap with me? | Brain | 1 (warn), 2 (claims) |
| Collaboration | Handoff, shared notes, subagent result merge | Brain | 2+ |

### Identity record

```jsonc
{
  "session_id": "083bcf79-…",            // Entire session id
  "parent_session_id": null,              // set for subagents (derived in Phase 1; see adapter)
  "continues_session_id": "54c0e4d4-…",   // CLI ask (d); null until it ships
  "agent_id": "ade8c9b2eec7e9193",        // host subagent id (subagents only)
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01E19…",          // links to checkpoint IsTask/ToolUseID (export.go:3798-3799)
  "kind": "session" | "subagent",
  "agent": "Claude Code", "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "subagent_type": "Explore",
  "description": "Map multi-agent primitives in brain",
  "branch": "feat/linear-issue-memory",
  "worktree": "C:/…/entire-brain/.claude/worktrees/trail197-findings",
  "worktree_confidence": "verified" | "reported"
}
```

`worktree_confidence` exists because the CLI-reported `worktree_path` can be wrong. Session
`586a7064` ran in `.claude/worktrees/trail197-findings` on branch `fix/trail197-findings`, yet its
state file reports the main checkout path. Brain verifies the path by matching the session's branch
against `git worktree list --porcelain`. When the two disagree, the branch match wins, and the
result is marked `reported` when it cannot be verified.

### Presence

Derived. No new daemon and no heartbeat writer in Phase 1.

| State | Rule |
|---|---|
| `active` | CLI status `active`, or `last_interaction_time` within 2 minutes |
| `idle` | Not ended, and last interaction within the stale window (default 30 minutes, `--stale-after`) |
| `stale` | Not ended, but older than the stale window. Shown only with `--all`. Never triggers warnings. |
| `ended` | `ended_at` is set. Hidden unless `--all`. |

Subagents inherit their parent's presence, and are `active` while the parent is not ended and the
subagent has no trustworthy `completed_at`. CLI ask (b) explains why `completed_at` is untrusted
today. Expiry by timeout, not by an end event, is deliberate: sessions crash and never send one.
This mirrors the stale rule in `memoryCoordinatorHealth` (`internal/cli/memory_coordinator.go:175-190`).

### Intent (observed)

For each distinct live worktree, Brain computes:

1. **Changed files.** This reuses the `brainLiveStateReport` machinery: `git status --porcelain`,
   filtered by `loadBrainIgnore`, plus `git diff --shortstat HEAD`. It is generalized to take any
   worktree path rather than only the caller's.
2. **Changed symbols.** Changed files map to entities through Graph's working-tree entity diff
   for that worktree (`entire graph diff`, working tree, not `--head`). Brain also uses the
   `changedSemanticFiles` path where an index exists. If Graph is unavailable, the result stays at
   file level with `granularity: "file"`.
3. **Task text.** From the CLI `last_prompt` for sessions and `task_description` for subagents.
   It is truncated to 120 characters and passed through the existing privacy exclusions.

**Brain never uses CLI `files_touched` or task-record `files` in Phase 1.** Both are wrong today
(see CLI ask (c)). Intent is attributed to a *worktree*, not to a session. When several live
sessions share one worktree, they share its diff, and the output says so (`shared_worktree: true`).
That limit is accepted for Phase 1.

## Interface

### `entire brain agents [--json] [--all] [--stale-after 30m] [--no-symbols]`

The human output is a tree grouped by worktree:

```
worktree .claude/worktrees/trail197-findings  (fix/trail197-findings)  4 files dirty
  ● 586a7064  Claude Code · opus-5-5  idle 12m  "resolve trail 197 review findings"
      changes: internal/issues/store.go (Import, State), internal/cli/issues.go (+2)
worktree .  (feat/linear-issue-memory)  1 file dirty
  ● 41205a80  Claude Code · opus-5-5  active  "open trail status + multiplayer"   ← you
      └ fork ab87ba50  "Finish trail 197 findings"  running
overlaps: none
```

The `--json` schema (`brain.agents/v1`):

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "brain.agents/v1",
  "generated_at": "…",
  "self_session_id": "41205a80-…",          // from ENTIRE_SESSION_ID / `entire session current`
  "source": { "cli_version": "0.11.3", "adapter": "state-files" | "cli-json", "warnings": [] },
  "worktrees": [{
    "path": "…", "branch": "…", "head": "…",
    "dirty": true, "changed_files": ["…"],
    "changed_symbols": [{ "file": "…", "name": "Import", "kind": "method", "change": "modified" }],
    "granularity": "symbol" | "file",
    "sessions": ["586a7064-…"], "shared_worktree": false
  }],
  "agents": [ /* identity record + */ {
    "presence": "active" | "idle" | "stale" | "ended",
    "last_interaction_at": "…", "children": ["<agent ids>"]
  }],
  "overlaps": [{
    "kind": "file" | "symbol",
    "target": "internal/issues/store.go" ,
    "worktrees": ["…", "…"], "sessions": ["…", "…"]
  }],
  "coverage": { "symbols": "complete" | "partial" | "none", "notes": [] }
}
```

`overlaps` lists files or symbols that are dirty in two or more live worktrees. It is computed only
between `active` and `idle` sessions.

### MCP `brain_agents`

This tool takes the same payload as `--json`. Its arguments are `include_stale` (bool) and
`symbols` (bool, default true). It is registered alongside `brain_brief` in `mcpToolDefinitions`
(`internal/cli/mcp.go:815`) and dispatched through `handleMCPToolCall` (`mcp.go:1034`). It is
read-only and has no workspace requirement.

### `brief`: "Concurrent work" section

`runBrainBrief` (`agent_surface.go:1362`) gains one section. It is emitted only when at least one
*other* live session exists and is relevant to the task, meaning its changed files or symbols
intersect the brief's located files or the caller's own diff:

```
Concurrent work (2 other live sessions)
- 586a7064 (fix/trail197-findings, idle 12m) is changing internal/issues/store.go: Import, State
  → overlaps your task's located file internal/issues/store.go
```

The section has a budget of 3 lines per session and 5 sessions at most, and the compact form
(`brain_brief_compact.go`) carries it as a `concurrent` record. It is silent when nothing is
relevant, following the same honesty rule as the rest of the brief.

Impact check: `runBrainBrief` has 3 direct and 2 transitive callers: the CLI command, MCP
`handleMCPToolCall`, and `runBrainBriefWithRawHistoryMatcher` (Graph impact, `--head` at `f423963d`).
The section is additive, so no caller contract changes. The compact v1 record set gains one record type.

### `hook pre-edit`: collision warning

`newHookPreEditCommand` (`internal/cli/hook_cmd.go:175`) is called only by `newHookCommand`, which
is mounted in `NewRootCommand` (Graph impact). It keeps its harness-safety contract (`hook_cmd.go:15-33`):
it is silent when there is nothing to say, never fails, is token-budgeted, and stays on the warm path.

- New behaviour: before the facts lookup, check whether `--file` is dirty in another *live*
  worktree. If it is, emit one line:
  `⚠ also being changed by 586a7064 (fix/trail197-findings, active 1m): "resolve trail 197…"`.
- Warm path: this check must not shell out per worktree on every edit. It reads a cached
  `agents` snapshot under the brain dir. The snapshot is refreshed when older than 15 seconds, and
  the refresh is bounded at 500 ms. If the bound is exceeded, the hook stays silent and logs a
  warning, as it already does today.
- The hook only warns and never blocks. An "ignore" override is not needed in Phase 1 because
  nothing is enforced.
- The hook warns at file level only. Symbol-level pre-edit waits for the worktree overlay seam
  (`docs/worktree_overlay_seam.md`), as the hook's own comment already notes.

## Data sources and the temporary adapter

The public JSON in Entire CLI 0.11.3 does not include subagents. Neither `entire session list --json`,
`session info --json` nor `entire status --json` returns `task_records`. Phase 1 therefore reads
behind a single interface:

```go
type liveSessionSource interface {
    Sessions(ctx context.Context) ([]liveSession, []string /*warnings*/, error)
}
```

- **`cliJSONSource`**: `entire session list --json`, plus `info --json` per live session. This
  is the preferred source, used once the CLI returns task records (ask (a)).
- **`stateFileSource`**: the temporary adapter, to be deleted when ask (a) ships. It reads
  `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` (via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, so every worktree sees
  the same set) and uses only these fields: `session_id, agent_type, model_name, branch,
  worktree_path, started_at, last_interaction_time, ended_at, phase, last_prompt, task_records[]{agent_id,
  tool_use_id, subagent_type, task_description, started_at, completed_at}`.
  - It ignores unknown fields.
  - It treats any parse error as a warning, never as a failure.
  - It gates on `cli_version` and records `adapter: "state-files"` in the output, so callers know
    which source answered.

The parent link is implicit, because the child record lives inside the parent's file. The adapter
emits `parent_session_id` from that containment.

## Failure modes

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Entire CLI missing, or unknown state schema | `agents` reports a single self entry with a warning, the brief section is omitted, and the hook stays silent |
| Crashed session never ends | It goes `stale` after the stale window and drops out of warnings |
| Background subagent `completed_at` stamped at launch | `completed_at` is ignored when it is within 1 s of `started_at`; presence is inherited from the parent |
| Wrong `worktree_path` | Branch match against `git worktree list` wins; marked `reported` otherwise |
| Two sessions in one worktree | Shared diff, `shared_worktree: true`, no per-session attribution |
| One conversation split into two sessions | Shown as two until ask (d); grouped when the transcript-path prefix matches (best effort, flagged) |
| Graph unavailable or slow | File granularity, `coverage.symbols: "none"` |
| Large monorepo or many worktrees | Bounded: 16 worktrees max, a per-worktree diff timeout, truncation reported |
| Privacy-excluded session | Omitted from task text and only counted, reusing the existing exclusions |

## Test plan

- **Unit:**
  - presence derivation: active, idle, stale and ended boundaries;
  - the `completed_at` sanity rule;
  - branch-over-path worktree verification;
  - overlap computation;
  - adapter parsing over recorded fixtures from 0.11.3 state files, including malformed, missing and
    unknown-field cases.
- **Integration** (temp repo with two `git worktree`s and fake session state files):
  - `agents --json` matches the golden output;
  - `brief` shows the Concurrent work section only when the work is relevant;
  - `hook pre-edit` warns for a file dirty in the other worktree and stays silent otherwise;
  - the warm-path latency budget is asserted.
- **MCP:** `brain_agents` is listed in `tools/list`, and the handler returns the schema.
- **Windows:** state-file reads go through the existing file-lock and atomic patterns (`filelock.go`).
  Paths are normalized with `filepath.ToSlash`.

## Benchmark lane

This adds a lane to `benchmarks/agent-brain` called **parallel-overlap**:

- **Setup:** N = 2–4 agents get overlapping tasks on one repository at the same time, in separate
  worktrees.
- **Arms:** Brain off, and Brain on with `brief` plus `hook pre-edit`.
- **Metrics:** merge conflicts at integration, duplicated edits to the same symbol, rework commits,
  wall-clock time, and the number of warnings shown versus acted on.
- **Phase 1 bar:** fewer conflicts and duplicated edits than with Brain off, and a false-warning
  rate below 10%.

## Phase 0 exit criteria

- The ADR is accepted.
- The CLI team has acknowledged asks (a)–(d) (the asks doc).
- The decision is made on the open questions below.

## Open questions

1. How long should the stale window be by default? 30 minutes is proposed.
2. Should `hook pre-edit` warn on `idle` sessions or only `active` ones? Proposed: both, labelled.
3. Should the brief show concurrent sessions on *other* branches that touch the same files?
   Proposed: yes, because that is where silent merge conflicts come from.
4. Should Codex sessions be in scope for Phase 1? Their subagent hooks differ.

Brain had no index for this repository, so recorded history came from `entire search`:

- **Session `de272aad` (2026-08-17, checkpoint `fb8977eb`).** It surveyed an external prototype of a
  local coordination layer for already-running agents (messaging, agent registry, symbol-level
  claims, handoffs, leases), and concluded that the ecosystem lacked agent-to-agent coordination
  and semantic collision detection. It recommended that as the reference design for claims
  (Phase 2+), and noted CLI subagent parent/child work (entireio/cli PR #1570). The session's author

- **June 2026 "workspace Radar" commits** (`19d74591` "test: retain workspace Radar no-claim
  evidence", `cd13cb0f`). These are Regression Radar and benchmark claim policy, not agent claims,
  so they are unrelated to this design.
- **PR #267, coordinated agent instructions** (session `01a09c53`, 2026-09-13). This covers agent

- **Sessions `54c0e4d4` and `083bcf79` (2026-10-03).** These established the five-layer plan and

# ADR 0001: Ownership of multiplayer agent awareness, and advisory coordination

- Status: proposed
- Date: 2026-10-03
- Context doc: [`docs/multiplayer_agents_design.md`](../multiplayer_agents_design.md)

This is the repository's first ADR. Later records follow this numbering and format: Status, Date,
Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives.

## Context

Brain should see the agents working in a repository: sessions, subagents, and what each is changing.
It should also warn before two of them collide. Two questions shape everything after:

1. **Who owns the live registry** of sessions, meaning identity and presence?
2. **Are collision controls enforced**, through locks, **or advisory**, through warnings and claims?

On the first question:

- **The Entire CLI already captures sessions across worktrees.** For each session it records the
  agent, model, branch, worktree, last prompt and interaction time. As of 0.11.3 it also records
  subagents under the parent session (`task_records` in `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json`, verified
  2026-10-03).
- **The CLI is installed in every agent harness** through its hooks.
- **Brain has the parts that use this data, and none that capture it.** It has the semantic index,
  Graph integration, facts and memory, the brief and hook surfaces, and lease/heartbeat patterns
  (`memory_coordinator.go`) and cross-process locks (`filelock.go`). It has no session capture of its
  own. It only reads committed checkpoints (`export.go:41-50`).

On the second question: hard locks between autonomous agents tend to deadlock, and locks left by
crashed agents block work. Agents also legitimately need to touch "someone else's" file
(refactors, merges).

## Decision

1. **The Entire CLI owns identity and presence.** It owns the session record, the parent/child
   links, the conversation continuation link, the worktree, and liveness. Brain consumes these
   through the CLI's public JSON. Until that JSON carries subagents, Brain reads the CLI's state
   files through one isolated adapter. That adapter is deleted when the public JSON catches up.
   Brain does not build a second session tracker.
2. **Brain owns intent, collision detection and memory.** That covers:
   - mapping each live worktree's diff to symbols via Graph;
   - computing overlaps;
   - the `agents` command and MCP tool;
   - the brief's "Concurrent work" section and the `hook pre-edit` warning;
   - later, claims, handoff and retaining coordination outcomes as facts.
3. **Brain derives intent from observation, not self-report.** Phase 1 uses only the worktree's
   git diff. The CLI's `files_touched` and task-record `files` are not used until they are
   accurate.
4. **Coordination is advisory.** Brain warns and never blocks an edit, commit or tool call. When
   Phase 2 adds declared claims, they will:
   - be advisory and expire through a heartbeat timeout;
   - be overridable by explicit action;
   - log each override as reviewable evidence.

   No hard locks between agents.

## Consequences

- Brain depends on CLI changes to reach the full design. The four asks are listed in
  `docs/multiplayer_cli_phase0_asks.md`. Phase 1 can ship on 0.11.3 with the adapter and
  documented limits.
- The adapter is coupled to an internal CLI file format. That risk is accepted and contained in
  three ways:
  - it is a single file;
  - it ignores unknown fields and gates on CLI version;
  - it degrades to a warning, never an error.
- Intent is attributed per worktree. Several sessions in one worktree cannot be told apart in
  Phase 1.
- Advisory warnings can be ignored. Success is measured by the parallel-overlap benchmark lane,
  not assumed.
- Cross-machine presence (Phase 3) will need a hosted endpoint with server-side expiry, and an
  agreed privacy boundary for what leaves the machine. This ADR does not decide either.

## Alternatives considered

- **Brain runs its own session tracker** (from `memory notify` hints and a heartbeat file). It was
  rejected because it duplicates the CLI and the two would drift. It would also need its own hooks
  in every harness. The hint stream (`memory_state.go:66`) stays a memory-lifecycle signal.
- **A shared standalone daemon.** It was rejected for now because there is no daemon support on
  Windows and a daemon adds an install and operations burden. It can be revisited for Phase 3.
- **Enforced locks.** These were rejected because of deadlock, stale-lock recovery and legitimate
  cross-ownership edits. External prior art surveyed in session `de272aad` (2026-08-17) pairs
  claims with expiry and override for the same reason.
- **Trusting the CLI's `files_touched`.** This was rejected because it is demonstrably wrong today.
  Every session and subagent on this machine reports the same 26 unrelated files.

# ADR 0001: Ownership of multiplayer agent awareness, and advisory coordination

- Status: proposed
- Date: 2026-10-03
- Context doc: [`docs/multiplayer_agents_design.md`](../multiplayer_agents_design.md)

This is the repository's first ADR. Later records follow this numbering and format: Status, Date,
Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives.

## Context

Brain should see the agents working in a repository: sessions, subagents, and what each is changing.
It should also warn before two of them collide. Two questions shape everything after:

1. **Who owns the live registry** of sessions, meaning identity and presence?
2. **Are collision controls enforced**, through locks, **or advisory**, through warnings and claims?

On the first question:

- **The Entire CLI already captures sessions across worktrees.** For each session it records the
  agent, model, branch, worktree, last prompt and interaction time. As of 0.11.3 it also records
  subagents under the parent session (`task_records` in `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json`, verified
  2026-10-03).
- **The CLI is installed in every agent harness** through its hooks.
- **Brain has the parts that use this data, and none that capture it.** It has the semantic index,
  Graph integration, facts and memory, the brief and hook surfaces, and lease/heartbeat patterns
  (`memory_coordinator.go`) and cross-process locks (`filelock.go`). It has no session capture of its
  own. It only reads committed checkpoints (`export.go:41-50`).

On the second question: hard locks between autonomous agents tend to deadlock, and locks left by
crashed agents block work. Agents also legitimately need to touch "someone else's" file
(refactors, merges).

## Decision

1. **The Entire CLI owns identity and presence.** It owns the session record, the parent/child
   links, the conversation continuation link, the worktree, and liveness. Brain consumes these
   through the CLI's public JSON. Until that JSON carries subagents, Brain reads the CLI's state
   files through one isolated adapter. That adapter is deleted when the public JSON catches up.
   Brain does not build a second session tracker.
2. **Brain owns intent, collision detection and memory.** That covers:
   - mapping each live worktree's diff to symbols via Graph;
   - computing overlaps;
   - the `agents` command and MCP tool;
   - the brief's "Concurrent work" section and the `hook pre-edit` warning;
   - later, claims, handoff and retaining coordination outcomes as facts.
3. **Brain derives intent from observation, not self-report.** Phase 1 uses only the worktree's
   git diff. The CLI's `files_touched` and task-record `files` are not used until they are
   accurate.
4. **Coordination is advisory.** Brain warns and never blocks an edit, commit or tool call. When
   Phase 2 adds declared claims, they will:
   - be advisory and expire through a heartbeat timeout;
   - be overridable by explicit action;
   - log each override as reviewable evidence.

   No hard locks between agents.

## Consequences

- Brain depends on CLI changes to reach the full design. The four asks are listed in
  `docs/multiplayer_cli_phase0_asks.md`. Phase 1 can ship on 0.11.3 with the adapter and
  documented limits.
- The adapter is coupled to an internal CLI file format. That risk is accepted and contained in
  three ways:
  - it is a single file;
  - it ignores unknown fields and gates on CLI version;
  - it degrades to a warning, never an error.
- Intent is attributed per worktree. Several sessions in one worktree cannot be told apart in
  Phase 1.
- Advisory warnings can be ignored. Success is measured by the parallel-overlap benchmark lane,
  not assumed.
- Cross-machine presence (Phase 3) will need a hosted endpoint with server-side expiry, and an
  agreed privacy boundary for what leaves the machine. This ADR does not decide either.

## Alternatives considered

- **Brain runs its own session tracker** (from `memory notify` hints and a heartbeat file). It was
  rejected because it duplicates the CLI and the two would drift. It would also need its own hooks
  in every harness. The hint stream (`memory_state.go:66`) stays a memory-lifecycle signal.
- **A shared standalone daemon.** It was rejected for now because there is no daemon support on
  Windows and a daemon adds an install and operations burden. It can be revisited for Phase 3.
- **Enforced locks.** These were rejected because of deadlock, stale-lock recovery and legitimate
  cross-ownership edits. External prior art surveyed in session `de272aad` (2026-08-17) pairs
  claims with expiry and override for the same reason.
- **Trusting the CLI's `files_touched`.** This was rejected because it is demonstrably wrong today.
  Every session and subagent on this machine reports the same 26 unrelated files.
